newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims steady in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims steady in latest week.

text.p: The number of people signing up for new state unemployment benefits last week remained unchanged from the previous week at 340,000, the Labour Department said Thursday.
The total was just below the Wall Street forecast of 341,000.
However, the department's four-week moving average of jobless claims, which is considered a more accurate measurement of employment trends, inched upward for the seventh consecutive week.
The average rose to 334,500 in the week ended Sept. 28 from 328,750 the week before. It was the highest reading since an average of 312,500 claims for the week ended June 10, 1996.
The department said four states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Sept. 21, the latest period for which the data are available.
They were North Carolina, with 1,990 fewer claims; New York, with 1,886; Illinois, with 1,697; and Tennessee, with 1,075.
North Carolina cited fewer layoffs in the construction and textile industries. Illinois had fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and manufacturing.
Tennessee had fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel, lumber, leather goods, electronic and transportation equipment, and service industries. New York had no comment.
Labour said Michigan and Puerto Rico reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the September 21 week.
Michigan, with 1,310 additional claims, cited layoffs in the automobile industry, while Puerto Rico, with 8,638 more filings, attributed the rise to the impact of Hurricane Hortense.
